outcome.answer: The closest match is a paper about checking how search-answer behavior changes when the retrieval tool is modified, but it is about refusal signals, not removing a page to see how the answer changes [6]. Another paper studies search APIs as decision surfaces and compares how different evidence and rankings affect agent answers, which is related to external search results but not specifically page-removal tests [1]. A broader paper on reliability and misinformation in search-backed answers also evaluates groundedness and source credibility, but it does not describe the page-removal method you asked about [9].
